g.text: L1 (in-process MemoryCache, microseconds) + L2 (Redis, milliseconds) + stampede protection (factory runs ONCE under concurrent miss) + tag-based invalidation.
invalidate AFTER the save, not before.
If you invalidate first, a concurrent reader sees the stale row → repopulates the cache with the OLD value → your save commits → cache is now stale for the L1 TTL.
Invalidate AFTER save closes that window. The 5-min TTL is only the safety net.
⚠ Multi-replica L1 invalidation: NOT IMPLEMENTED in HybridCache 10.x
Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Hybrid 10.x has NO backplane. RemoveByTagAsync clears L2
+ the calling replica's L1 — but other replicas keep serving stale L1 for the
FINE TODAY: we run single-replica via Aspire.
1. Cheap fix: drop LocalCacheExpiration to 60s (one-line) → bounded staleness.
2. Real fix: migrate to FusionCache — ships a Redis pub/sub backplane that notifies
all replicas to clear L1. Tracked in STATUS.md.
private static readonly HybridCacheEntryOptions Options = new() { Expiration = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5), LocalCacheExpiration = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5) };
public Task<ProductDto?> GetOrLoadAsync(Guid id, Func<CancellationToken, Task<ProductDto?>> factory, CancellationToken ct = default)
=> cache.GetOrCreateAsync(KeyFor(id), async cancel => await factory(cancel), options: Options, tags: [TagFor(id)], cancellationToken: ct).AsTask();
